programs.name: DEERS (Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System)
programs.eligibility: All uniformed service members (active, retired, Reserve/Guard) are registered automatically. Eligible family members (spouse, children, certain dependents) must be registered by the sponsor to receive TRICARE and other DoD benefits.
programs.coverage: DEERS is the DoD database that determines eligibility for TRICARE health care, the military ID card, and other benefits. Dependents must be enrolled and kept current. Sponsors add/update family members via milConnect, ID Card Office Online, or a local ID card/RAPIDS office (DD Form 1172-2 required to add a member).
programs.notes: Check your DEERS record at least once every three months; outdated info causes denied or delayed TRICARE claims, referrals, and prescriptions. DMDC/DEERS Support Office: 800-538-9552.

programs.name: Uniformed Services (Dependent) ID Card
programs.eligibility: Eligible family members registered in DEERS. Dependent children generally must be ID-carded at age 10 (some exceptions allow earlier issuance).
programs.coverage: The Uniformed Services ID card provides installation access and verifies eligibility for TRICARE, commissary, and exchange benefits. Apply online via ID Card Office Online or in person at a RAPIDS site (appointments recommended). Required: a completed DD Form 1172-2 signed by the sponsor, two forms of ID, and proof of relationship.
programs.notes: Enroll the dependent in DEERS first; the sponsor must be present or have pre-signed the DD Form 1172-2 (or granted a power of attorney) for the appointment.

programs.name: Adding Dependents to VA Disability Compensation (VA Form 21-686c)
programs.eligibility: Veterans eligible for VA disability compensation with a combined disability rating of at least 30%. Qualifying dependents: a spouse, unmarried children under 18 (or 18–23 if in school full-time, or permanently disabled before 18), and dependent parents in the veteran's direct care who meet income/net-worth limits.
programs.coverage: A veteran rated 30% or higher receives additional monthly compensation for eligible dependents. Add, remove, or update dependents online at va.gov/manage-dependents or via VA Form 21-686c (dependent parents use VA Form 21P-509).
programs.notes: File within one year of the marriage, birth, or adoption (if already rated 30%+ at the time) to receive benefits retroactive to that event date.

programs.name: Marriage — Update DEERS & VA Benefits
programs.eligibility: A spouse becomes TRICARE-eligible once registered in DEERS. For VA, a veteran rated 30% or higher can add a spouse as a dependent for additional compensation.
programs.coverage: TRICARE health coverage for the spouse; increased monthly VA disability compensation when a spouse is added (only at 30%+ rating).
programs.notes: Marriage is a TRICARE Qualifying Life Event giving a 90-day window from the marriage date to register the spouse in DEERS and enroll in a plan. DEERS and VA are separate systems — do both.

programs.name: New Child / Adoption — Add to DEERS & VA
programs.eligibility: A newborn or newly adopted/court-placed child of a sponsor; the child must be registered in DEERS. For VA, a veteran rated 30% or higher can add the child as a dependent.
programs.coverage: TRICARE coverage for the child once enrolled; increased VA disability compensation for a dependent child (at 30%+ rating).
programs.notes: Birth/adoption is a Qualifying Life Event with a 90-day window (120 days overseas) to register the child in DEERS and enroll in a plan; claims aren't paid after the window. Add the child to VA disability separately on VA.gov.

programs.name: Divorce — Remove Former Spouse from DEERS (20/20/20 Rule)
programs.eligibility: A former spouse's TRICARE ends on the date of divorce UNLESS they qualify as an unremarried former spouse: 20/20/20 = sponsor has 20+ years creditable service, 20+ years of marriage, and all 20 marriage years overlap the service years (full TRICARE). 20/20/15 = same but only 15 years overlap (one year of transitional coverage).
programs.coverage: Loss of TRICARE/ID privileges for a non-qualifying former spouse; full retiree-equivalent TRICARE for 20/20/20 former spouses (lost upon remarriage).
programs.notes: The sponsor must update DEERS with a certified copy of the divorce decree. Children keep eligibility. A qualifying 20/20/20 former spouse who remarries permanently loses the benefit.

programs.name: Transfer Post-9/11 GI Bill to Dependents (TEB)
programs.eligibility: An active-duty or Selected Reserve service member who, on the approval date, has completed at least 6 years of service AND agrees to add 4 more. The dependent receiving benefits must be enrolled in DEERS.
programs.coverage: Up to 36 months of Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) entitlement transferable to a spouse and/or children.
programs.notes: The transfer MUST be requested while still serving, via milConnect — you cannot start one after leaving service. A spouse can use benefits after 6 years of service; a child only after 10 years.

programs.name: Report the Veteran's Death to VA
programs.eligibility: Any survivor or legal representative of a deceased veteran may report the death. The one-time 'month of death' payment is payable only if the veteran was receiving VA compensation or pension at the time of death.
programs.coverage: Reporting the death stops the veteran's benefit payments (preventing overpayment debt) and triggers redirection of benefits. A surviving spouse may be paid the amount of compensation/pension the veteran would have received for the month in which the veteran died.
programs.notes: Calling is fastest: 800-827-1000 (option 5). Report promptly to avoid overpayment debt. Unpaid benefits owed at death (accrued benefits) are claimed separately via VA Form 21P-601.

programs.name: Apply for DIC / Survivors Pension
programs.eligibility: Surviving spouse, child, or parent of a service member who died in the line of duty, or of a veteran who died from a service-connected condition. Marriage-duration and other rules apply. Survivors Pension is a separate needs-based benefit for low-income survivors.
programs.coverage: A tax-free monthly monetary benefit to eligible survivors.
programs.notes: A surviving spouse/child files VA Form 21P-534EZ; a survivor of an active-duty member files 21P-534a with a casualty assistance officer. One application covers DIC, Survivors Pension, and accrued benefits.

programs.name: Burial Benefits, Burial Flag, and Headstone/Marker
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — National Cemetery Administration
programs.eligibility: Eligible veterans and certain family members. A headstone/marker/medallion may be applied for by a family member, personal representative, VSO, qualifying official, or the person responsible for the remains.
programs.coverage: A burial allowance (funeral/burial/transport costs), a gravesite in a VA national cemetery, a government headstone/marker/medallion, a burial flag, and a Presidential Memorial Certificate — at no cost to the family.
programs.notes: Burial flag: VA Form 27-2008. Headstone/marker: VA Form 40-1330. Headstone help line: 800-697-6947; burial scheduling: 800-535-1117.

programs.name: Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) Annuity Activation
programs.eligibility: A surviving spouse (or former spouse/child) of a deceased military retiree who had SBP coverage in effect; surviving spouses are eligible for the SBP annuity for life.
programs.coverage: An inflation-adjusted monthly lifetime annuity based on a percentage of the retiree's pay.
programs.notes: First report the retiree's death to DFAS at 800-321-1080; DFAS then mails the SBP claim package. The surviving spouse activates the annuity with DD Form 2656-7. Payments typically begin about 45–60 days after death if paperwork is prompt.

programs.name: Survivor Education & Health Benefits (CHAMPVA, DEA, Fry Scholarship)
programs.eligibility: DEA (Chapter 35): spouse/child of a veteran who died, is captured/missing, or is permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition. Fry Scholarship: child or surviving spouse of a service member who died in the line of duty on or after 9/11/2001. CHAMPVA: survivor of a veteran who died of (or was P&T-rated for) a service-connected disability, or who died in the line of duty.
programs.coverage: DEA: monthly education and job-training assistance. Fry Scholarship: tuition, housing, books, and supplies. CHAMPVA: health coverage for medically necessary services.
programs.notes: A survivor generally cannot use both DEA and the Fry Scholarship for the same period — compare which gives more before electing. These benefits also appear on the Federal Benefits and Family/Survivor/Retiree Benefits pages.
